what_happened: The job routed the producer's cargo build, test, clippy and check commands through the build-slot. The verifier rejected it at the final verdict. One of 7 acceptance criteria was unmet: a test must show `cargo fmt` and `cargo metadata` run through the wrapper without taking a slot, even when every slot is held. There were two findings. The major one: the evidence for behavior criterion 4 must cite commands that ran (D43), and it did not. The blocker: `cargo test` fails because the new test file is not registered in the checked-in shard timings file xtask/shard-timings.txt. The test check failed. Its recorded output shows only CI checkout cleanup and a Node.js 20 warning, so it names no test. That failed check is separate from the unmet criterion.
cause: A repo rule requires every new test file to be listed in xtask/shard-timings.txt. That rule lives only in a test that runs at the end, and neither the request, the reading nor the producer's instructions mention it. The producer therefore had no way to know to register the file, and the first run of the test check is the final verdict. The check output kept in the event is only CI cleanup noise, so the producer and verifier could not see which test failed. The criterion about evidence from commands that ran also depends on the producer reporting commands the verifier cannot observe, which is the same blind spot seen in earlier jobs.
prevention: Add a fast code check that runs in the producer's loop, and again before the verifier. It fails when any test file in the repo is missing from xtask/shard-timings.txt, and its message names the file and the line to add. Also keep the real failing test name and assertion in the recorded test-check output, not just the CI cleanup tail. Together these catch the whole class: a missing registration is reported while the producer can still fix it.
proposed_request: Make the missing test-file registration a fast, early failure. Outcome: when a test file exists that is not listed in xtask/shard-timings.txt, the producer's local checks and Athena's pre-verifier checks fail at once with a message naming the unregistered file and the line to add. Acceptance: (1) a test creates a temporary test file that is not registered and shows the check fails and names that file; (2) a test shows the check passes when every test file is registered; (3) when the test check fails, the recorded output keeps the failing test name and assertion text, not only the CI checkout cleanup lines; (4) `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets` and `cargo test` pass from the repo root, and the evidence cites the commands that ran. Then retry the build-slot job (20261106-002344-jn5t) with its own unmet criterion kept: a test that shows `cargo fmt` and `cargo metadata` run through the wrapper without taking a slot even when every slot is held, and the new test file registered in xtask/shard-timings.txt.
